title: Jensen Huang broke Nvidia’s code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it
lede: Jensen Huang admitted at his first all-hands since returning as Nvidia CEO that he broke the company's code of conduct, and ethics experts say the likely cost is cultural rather than legal.

points: Huang told staff the code binds everyone, but that a breach does not mean automatic dismissal, since facts and circumstances still count, Wired reported.
Matt Plass of compliance firm LRN, who surveyed more than 2,000 workers, says the main risk is employees growing ashamed of where they work.
Plass recalls a CEO who appeared in an Olympics VIP box during a company travel ban, an episode staff cited as the benchmark of bad behaviour for over a decade.
The usual fix of replacing the leader and apologising is harder at Nvidia, which has no clear succession plan and is closely identified with Huang.
An employee campaign for his reinstatement suggests morale has held so far.
